Proposed quarter focus (3 themes): 1) Guided activation for non‑technical users — role-based, step‑by‑step setup that walks teams from “connect data” → “first dashboard” → “schedule report”; 2) Quick‑start templates & packaged metrics — industry/role templates (ops, finance, sales) with one‑click dashboards, queries, and alerts to shorten time‑to‑value; 3) Team engagement primitives — in‑app task nudges, automated weekly summary emails, and lightweight admin controls to drive habitual use and make expansion conversations obvious.  
How these move the needle: guided activation reduces early drop‑off and increases 14‑day activation, templates produce immediate value to convert new seats into weekly active users, and engagement primitives create repeat touchpoints that surface expansion opportunities.  
Key assumptions: most low engagement happens in the first 2–4 weeks after data connection; less‑technical ops/managers will use curated templates if they preserve key customization; engineering can commit to 2–3 medium‑scope projects this quarter.  
Open questions to finalize scope and targets: which customer segments (verticals, org roles, deal sizes) we prioritize first, what concrete numeric targets leadership wants for activation/WAU/expansion, and whether any security/integration policies limit shipping template bundles or email summaries.  
Next steps I recommend: 2‑week design+eng scoping for Guided Activation + one template pack, recruit 3 pilot customers for usability testing, and return with scoped work, resource estimates, and proposed KPI targets for approval.

Recommendation (capacity = two M/L + one S): fund Guided Activation Wizard (Large) and Ops + B2B‑SaaS Quick‑Start Template Pack (Medium), plus a Lightweight Engagement Primitives effort (Small); defer a Robust Alerting overhaul (Large) and broader multi‑vertical template expansion (Medium).  
Guided Wizard: role‑based first‑week flow (connect → map key fields → build-first-dashboard → schedule/share) with progress/checklist and activation telemetry; Template Pack: two pilot domain packs (logistics, B2B SaaS) with one‑click dashboards, mapped metrics and simple data‑mapping scripts; Engagement: in‑app nudges, admin checklist, and automated weekly summary emails.

Risky assumptions needing discovery: target segments (logistics, B2B SaaS) have mappable schemas and connector coverage; non‑technical ops will accept curated templates without heavy customization; email summaries meet privacy/compliance; we can accurately instrument activation/WAU metrics quickly.

rounds.response:
Plan (by week): Weeks 1–2: UX discovery/specs + Product-led pilot recruitment (UX/Product/Sales); Weeks 3–6: Engineering builds Wizard MVP, single‑vertical template alpha and instrumentation (Eng/Product/UX); Weeks 7–10: pilot rollouts (3 logistics, 3 B2B SaaS) with 1:1 enablement, weekly metrics & rapid fixes (CS/Sales/Product); Weeks 11–12: iterate on pilot feedback and decide limited GA and rollout sequence.  
Decision checkpoints: end W2 go/no‑go on core scope & chosen vertical; end W6 alpha review & instrumentation sign‑off (connect→dashboard flow must work and telemetry present); W8 pilot mid‑review to reprioritize fixes; W10 pilot evaluation = go/no‑go for limited GA.  
Explicit deferrals / “say no” items this quarter: multi‑table joins, advanced mapping UI, second vertical/template expansion, automated weekly emails, expansion‑scoring, robust alerting — and decline ad‑hoc template/custom connector requests or cosmetic UI churn outside hero flows.  
Sales/CS timing & messaging: position as an “early access guided setup + ops‑tuned templates” pilot today and promise usable guided flow + templates starting Week 7; only market as standard GA after W10 go‑decision and KPI progress toward ~+20ppt activation uplift / +1 WAU per account, otherwise call it pilot/early access.  
Design cadence & hero journeys: UX delivers stable designs for the hero path (connect → auto‑map top fields → first dashboard → schedule/share + admin checklist) by end W4 with engineering freeze start W5; if further capacity pressure arises we will hard‑freeze to the connect→dashboard→share MVP and single vertical templates.

rounds.response: We will protect the core quarter commitments (Wizard + focused Template Pack + Engagement/Instrumentation) as top priority and only accept other work under strict, pre‑defined categories. Priority categories: (1) P0 production incidents — immediate; (2) Deal‑critical tweaks — only if they materially unblock a near‑term signature (impact documented, sponsor from Sales, <2 dev days estimate OR paid/accelerated commitment, and preferably generalizable); (3) UX/QoL improvements — only if they measurably improve one of our hero ops/manager journeys, validated in a quick UX triage, and scoped ≤3 dev days.
